text:
TITLE: Trapped in an Abusive Marriage
I (27F) am terrified of my husband. I'm currently in a domestic violence situation and I'm not sure how to get out.
  
I've been in this relationship for 10 years and I've been married for 5. We have two kids together. He's always been the primary caregiver and I've always been the one to take care of everything in the household. I've been a stay-at-home mom for the past 5 years. 
  
I've been feeling trapped and suffocated for a while now. He's always been controlling and possessive, but it's gotten worse over the past year or so. He's always monitoring my phone and computer activity, he's always checking in on me and making sure I'm doing what he wants me to do. He yells at me and belittles me in front of the kids. He's even started to hit me.
  
I've been feeling like I'm walking on eggshells all the time. I'm always afraid of what he's going to say or do next. I'm afraid of what he's going to do to me or the kids. I'm afraid of losing everything. 
  
I don't know how to get out of this situation. I don't know how to leave him. I don't know how to take care of myself and the kids on my own. I'm scared of what will happen to us if I leave. 
  
For anyone else in this situation like this, how did you get out of it? What did you do to take care of yourself and your loved ones? Please help me. I'm desperate. 
  
Edit: I'm not looking for advice on how to make it work. I'm looking for advice on how to get out of it safely and how to take care of myself and my kids. Please be honest and please be kind. I'm begging you.

text:
TITLE: I am furious after being catcalled by a stranger
I’m a 24 year old non-binary person, and I was walking home from class today when a middle-aged man yelled out to me from across the street. I immediately felt my anxiety spike and my heart racing. I tried to ignore him and keep walking, but he continued to follow me, saying that I “look so sexy.” I finally had to quicken my pace to get away from him.
  
I am shaking from anger as I write this. I need to scream. catcalling is not okay, but it’s not just the catcalling itself that bothers me - it’s the fact that it’s so normalized. Every time I walk down the street, I’m putting myself at risk of being harassed or objectified. And it’s not just me - I know that so many other women and non-binary people have to deal with this kind of thing all the time.
  
people need to realize that catcalling is not a compliment, it’s not a form of flattery. It’s a way of asserting power and control over someone else’s body. And it’s not okay. I wish that people would stop doing it and start respecting people’s boundaries. Catcalling is not a harmless joke, it’s a form of harassment that can have serious consequences.
  
I don’t know how to process everything. I’m not alone in this feeling, and I hope that others will join me in speaking out against catcalling and harassment.

text:
TITLE: I'm 3 years out from anorexia recovery and it's weird
I was diagnosed with anorexia when I was 19. I was hospitalized for a while and then went to outpatient treatment for about a year. I'm 22 now and I've been in recovery for 3 years. It's weird because I'm finally starting to realize the impact it had on my life. I'm not just talking about the obvious things like weight gain and hair loss, I'm talking about the way it made me feel about myself and my worth. 
  
I used to think that I was worthless and that I deserved to be punished. I used to believe that I was too much for people to handle, that I was too loud, too opinionated, too emotional. I thought I was a burden and that I was only taking up space.
  
But now, I'm starting to see that those thoughts were lies. I now see that I was never a mistake, that I was never a burden. I am worthy of love and respect, not just from others, but from myself. 
  
It's weird because I'm finally starting to feel like myself again.
  
I'm not saying that I'm cured, but I finally feel like I deserve to exist as I am.
 
To anyone else who is struggling with an eating disorder, I see you. I hear you. I believe you. You are not alone. You are not a mistake. You are worthy of love and respect from others and yourself. You are worthy of taking up space. You are worthy of being alive. 
  
Edit: thank you to everyone who has commented. Your support means the world to me. I'm glad that I can be a source of hope for you. I'm glad that I can be a reminder that recovery is possible and that you are not alone.
